newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks mixed, dollar rises on Rubin.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks mixed, dollar rises on Rubin.

text.p: European stock markets opened mixed on Friday morning, focusing on earnings reports from local companies before the monthly U.S. jobs report due later in the day.

The dollar hovered just below 7-1/2 year highs against the mark and briefly touched an 11-week peak versus the yen after U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated his support for a strong dollar late on Thursday.
"We have always said we believe a strong dollar is in our interest," Rubin told Reuters in an interview.
The dollar initially gained on Rubin's remarks but eased off its highs by midmorning as traders awaited the July U.S. employment data due at 1230 GMT.
A Reuters survey forecasts non-farm payrolls up 193,000 from the previous month's 217,000 jump, with the unemployment rate edging down to 4.9 percent from 5.0 percent.
Average hourly earnings were seen gaining 0.2 percent after June's 0.3-percent rise. The average workweek was expected to slip to 34.6 hours from 34.7.
But until the jobs data are released, European share traders were more focused on domestic earnings reports.
In London, the FTSE-100 index shrugged off the Dow Jones Industrial Average's 32.28-point drop to 8,222.61 on Thursday to start firmer.
The FTSE benefited from a jump in Lloyds TSB Group Plc shares after the company reported a 33-percent increase in first-half, pre-tax profits.
Lloyd's shares rose more than 30 pence in early trade to hit a high of 707 before slipping back slightly.
French shares pared early gains but traders expected losses to be limited as long as the dollar remained strong, making French goods cheaper abroad and boosting exports.
Alcatel Alsthom was among the major winners, soaring about nine percent to a year high at 885 francs after the firm said first-half sales rose 17 percent.
But traders expected turnover to remain modest before the U.S. jobs report and as the market consolidated recent gains to record peaks.
Germany's blue-chip DAX index fell, weighed down by Daimler-Benz AG after two investment banks cut their earnings estimates for the company.

Merrill Lynch and Morgan Stanley downgraded Daimler's 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates despite the company's more than doubling of its operating profit in its six-month earnings report. At mid-morning, Daimler shares were down 7.5 marks at 147.30.
Finnish shares opened slighly lower, with Nokia easing as investors sold to lock in profits from the stock's recent rise before the company reports second-quarter results in Monday.
"The result is expected to be good, but the share has risen so much after Ericsson's results (last week) that some profit-taking could emerge today, or at least on Monday," a broker said.
Last week, Ericsson said first-half, pre-tax profits were 6.1 billion crowns ($763.5 million), outpacing average expectations for 5.11 billion crowns.
Dutch shares opened firmer, pulled up by Unilever Plc's four-for-one stock split, announced before the opening.
"I did not know a share split was coming up, although we could have expected that with the high share price," one dealer said.

Unilever also said first-half profits, including a 7.92-billion guilder ($3.8 billion) pre-tax profit from selling its chemical business, amounted to 9.2 billion. Its shares hit a year high of 1,810 in morning trade.
Switzerland's bourse is closed for a holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8455 marks and 118.75 yen from 1.8380 and 118.40 yen in late trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 3.7 points at 4,911.20.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index lost 32.75 points in bourse trade at 4,406.18.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 7.46 points at 3,068.21.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in morning London at $325.30, up from Thursday's close at $324.90. ($ = 7.989 Swedish Crowns) ($ = 2.079 Dutch Guilders)
